title: Florentine bargello cushion front
subtitle: A full 35 cm square cushion front in a four-row Florentine wave pattern on 13-count canvas
excerpt: A full-size 35 cm square cushion front in the Florentine bargello wave pattern. Six graduating shades of one colour fill the repeating wave rows. The upright stitches cover the canvas quickly, making this a satisfying large project for a confident beginner.
sourceNotes: Florentine wave pattern from Weldon's Practical Needlework, Florentine work series (1880s). Wave step and repeat proportions from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), flame stitch chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: The horizontal span of one complete peak-to-trough cycle in a Bargello pattern. The first row establishes the wave repeat; all subsequent rows follow the same outline.

heroPrompt: A square cushion on an armchair showing a rich Florentine bargello wave in six shades of coral to cream, natural light through a window, warm interior setting.

content.text: This cushion front is a 182 by 182 hole square on 13-count canvas, finishing at 35 by 35 cm. The Florentine wave uses stitches over four threads, stepping up or down two threads between adjacent stitches to form the characteristic ripple. Six shades of one colour: darkest to lightest and back: cycle through the rows. The first row sets the
wave repeat
; all other rows simply follow that outline.
What you need

content.text: Palette
Shade 1: DMC 356 / Anchor 5975: medium terra cotta
Shade 2: DMC 758 / Anchor 9575: light terra cotta
Shade 3: DMC 3722 / Anchor 1027: medium shell pink
Shade 4: DMC 3727 / Anchor 1016: light antique mauve
Shade 5: DMC 3716 / Anchor 25: very light dusty rose
Shade 6: DMC 712 / Anchor 926: cream
Stretching the canvas
A large scroll frame is essential. Bargello distorts the canvas less than tent stitch, but a cushion front of this size needs a stable working surface.
Stitches used
Bargello wave stitch
: upright stitches over four canvas threads, stepping up or down two threads between adjacent stitches.
Working method

Find the horizontal centre of the canvas (hole 91 of the 182-hole width). Work the first row of Shade 1 across the full width, starting from the centre and working outward to each side. Establish the full wave pattern in this first row. The wave repeat is 16 stitches wide (8 steps up to the peak, 8 steps down to the trough).
Work a second row of Shade 1 directly below the first, following the wave outline.
Work two rows each of Shades 2 through 6, then cycle back through 5 to 1 to reverse the gradient. This gives a symmetrical colour sequence across the full height.
Fill the full 182 by 182 hole area. Block by dampening and pinning square to a large board.
Finishing

Trim the canvas margin to 1.5 cm. Sew the backing fabric to the front, right sides facing, along three sides. Turn right side out. Insert the 35 cm cushion pad. Close the fourth side by hand with slip stitch.
What to try next
A two-colour variant alternates just two shades in each row. The result is bold and graphic on the same canvas and wave structure.
